clue.text: Somewhat lacking in intelligence? That's unfair

definitions.meaning: read literally, slightly dim or slow-witted
a British idiom for something unreasonable or more than one should have to put up with

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes someone slightly stupid, and as a British idiom it is a complaint that something is unreasonable.

clue.text: Saying book must be taken up for bed

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking the pieces up means reading the whole run from the foot to the head

parts.note: a motto is a short saying

explanation.surface: Someone insists on carrying a book of proverbs upstairs to read at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be taken up' turns the whole run MOTTO plus B, giving the answer in this down light. The bed is that of a sea or river, not the one you sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed of a sea or river is its floor, the lowest part.

clue.text: Go round home and call it a day?

parts.note: to go round is to turn, as a wheel does
in means at home, as in 'is she in?'

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stroll past the house and then decides they have done enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire to sleep for the night is to finish the day's activity, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Son occupying one type of accommodation or another

indicators.note: the son takes up a place inside the lodging word

parts.note: a hotel is a kind of place to stay
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A young man is living in one sort of lodging or possibly a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts S inside HOTEL. The definition 'another' leans back on the earlier words: a different type of accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a second kind of lodging, cheap shared rooms for travellers, as distinct from the first.

clue.text: Trick to get class to fall in line

parts.note: to con someone is to trick them
a form is a class or year group in a British school

explanation.surface: A teacher needs a ruse to make unruly pupils behave.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM is the British school word for a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are synonyms for complying with the rules or with what others do.

clue.text: Keep out of sight, certain to be reactionary

parts.note: to hide is to stay where you cannot be seen
bound means sure, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: Advice to stay hidden, since doing so is guaranteed to look backward-thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for someone rigidly opposed to change and stuck in old ways.

clue.text: Bishop, one subsequently gangster — having two sides!

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is the Roman numeral for one
later means afterwards
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, is crosswords' usual mobster

explanation.surface: A churchman who went on to become a mobster shows a double nature.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is Al Capone, the gangster crosswords reach for first.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something, such as a treaty or symmetry, that involves a pair of flanks or parties.

clue.text: Support golfer from remote country area

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
Tiger Woods is the American golfer

explanation.surface: Cheer on a golf player who comes from a far-off rural district.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names sparsely populated forest land far from towns.

clue.text: Tiny mother's lowest points

parts.note: mini means very small
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A very small mum's worst moments in life.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin plural for the smallest values, as of a curve's troughs.

clue.text: A time to get something for Christmas? That's now!

parts.note: a present is a gift, such as one given at Christmas

explanation.surface: The festive season is the moment to receive a gift, and it has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbial expressions meaning currently, at this moment.

clue.text: We'll roll round in grass in us city

indicators.note: the turned pronoun goes inside the word for an informer

parts.note: grass is British slang for a police informer, as is nark

indicators.note: rolling round turns the pronoun over so it reads backwards

parts.note: the pronoun we, with the contracted 'will' serving only the grammar

explanation.surface: People promise to tumble about on a lawn in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for a police informer, not the lawn the surface suggests. The clue prints US in lower case, hiding the country.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest municipality in the state of New Jersey.

clue.text: Cop lied about nothing with good companion of his?

indicators.note: about suggests the letters being thrown around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A dishonest officer told untruths over a trifle while with a decent partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' points back to the officer at the start of the clue, whose working partner this is; the question mark admits the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable's handler works alongside this trained animal, his partner on patrol.

clue.text: Former archbishop in pope's place with men around

parts.note: the Pope lives in Rome

indicators.note: around turns the soldiers' abbreviation to face the other way

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A one-time senior cleric stands in the Vatican with a crowd of people surrounding him.
explanation.walkthrough: Men are the army's other ranks, its ordinary soldiers. The archbishop is Oscar, of San Salvador, murdered in 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Romero was the prelate of San Salvador, assassinated in 1980.

clue.text: Country assistant's attempt to get starring role when about 50

parts.note: a stab is a try, as in 'have a stab at it'

indicators.note: the starring part goes round the numeral, which sits inside it

parts.note: the lead is the main part in a play or film
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A rural helper tries for the main part in a film at around the age of fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a worker who looks after horses in a racing yard, a rural helper.

clue.text: The female protecting relations notices unconventional youngsters

indicators.note: the pronoun shelters the family word by standing round it

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female
kin are one's relatives
ads are advertisements, public notices

explanation.surface: A woman shielding her family spots some rebellious teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'notices' is a verb, what the woman does; in the wordplay it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: They are members of a British youth subculture with shaven scalps and heavy boots.

clue.text: Defensive group made rough manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres are movements, so the letters shift into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military unit protecting a position carried out some clumsy exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges MADE ROUGH. The answer is Britain's Second World War volunteer force of local men, the 'Dad's Army'.
explanation.definitionFit: It was Britain's wartime volunteer militia formed to resist invasion.

clue.text: End of the script providing spaces for printer

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten or typed script

explanation.surface: The final page of a screenplay leaves blank gaps for the typesetter.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography these are units of width, each as wide as the type is high.

clue.text: Small creature, one airbrushed from electronic picture

indicators.note: airbrushing something from an image removes it

parts.note: an E-fit is a computer-made likeness of a suspect used by British police
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny animal has been digitally erased from a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airbrushed from' takes I out of EFIT. An E-fit is the computer-built picture of a suspect's face that British police issue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old name for a newt, especially a young one.

clue.text: Apprehensive cast

definitions.meaning: to throw, as at a coconut at a fairground

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning timid and also a verb or noun for a throw.

clue.text: Ape to go into space

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to mimic someone
what a rocket does on leaving the launch pad

explanation.surface: A monkey is to be launched on a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to mimic someone and to leave the ground, as a rocket does.

clue.text: Difficult to get hold of answer in official report

indicators.note: the word for difficult grips the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: It is tough to obtain a reply from a government document.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the printed word-for-word record of debates in the British Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the verbatim published record of proceedings in the British Parliament.

clue.text: Go in larder — take out pan

indicators.note: taking something out removes those letters from the longer word

parts.note: a pantry is a larder, a small room for storing food
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to enter the food cupboard and fetch a saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take out' removes PAN from PANTRY. 'Go' is a noun here: an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for an attempt, as in 'have a go'.

clue.text: Distinguished artist and famous actress meeting explorer

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
Vivien Leigh starred in Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A celebrated painter and a film star are introduced to an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts; LEIGH is Vivien Leigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter was the Elizabethan adventurer who sailed to the Americas.

clue.text: Type who's let us all down? That's a sure bet!

definitions.text: Type who's let us all down?
definitions.meaning: a financier, blamed by the public for the 2008 crash
British betting slang for a selection thought certain to win

explanation.surface: A person who disappointed everybody is nonetheless guaranteed to come good.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a financier, widely blamed for the crash, and in British betting slang a certainty.

clue.text: Troublemaker in port starts to turn everyone rebellious

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, crosswords' favourite

indicators.note: the starts of the words that follow are their opening letters

explanation.surface: An agitator at the docks begins to stir all the others into revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking part in violent public disorder is causing mayhem.

clue.text: German writer's work on anaesthetic cut short

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: cutting a word short removes its final letter

parts.note: ether was an early surgical anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A German author's book about pain relief was abridged.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the poet and dramatist who wrote Faust.

clue.text: One silly novel full of amorous emotion

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are muddled and out of their senses

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single daft romantic book brims with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smitten with another person is brimming with romantic feeling.

clue.text: Close in on fantastic enamelwork

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or bizarre, so the letters take a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Move nearer to admire some wonderful decorative metalwork.
explanation.definitionFit: It is decorative work in which coloured glaze fills cells divided by fine wire.

clue.text: Attractive person that's accepted by the pupil

definitions.meaning: as much as the organ of sight can take in, the pupil being part of it

explanation.surface: A good-looking individual wins the approval of a schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally it is a striking good-looker, and literally as much as one's organ of sight can take in.

clue.text: Speech in the office that comes from an autocrat?

definitions.meaning: words spoken by a boss for a secretary to take down
the giving of orders by a tyrant, whimsically, as he is a dictator

explanation.surface: A tyrannical boss delivers an address to the staff at work.
explanation.definitionFit: It is words spoken for a secretary to type, and whimsically the giving of orders by a tyrant.

clue.text: Trees? A landowner's getting groups of two and three chopped

indicators.text: getting groups of two and three chopped
indicators.note: a run of two letters and then a run of three are cut out of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
the two letters AN and the three letters OWN are the groups removed

explanation.surface: An estate holder is having clumps of woodland felled, a couple here and a trio there.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'groups' are runs of letters, not clumps of trees: a pair and then a trio are cut from the estate holder's word.
explanation.definitionFit: They are a kind of waterside timber plant of the birch family, an example.

clue.text: Hired as a professional accountant?

definitions.meaning: rented for private use, as a plane or boat is
the British title for a fully qualified member of an accountancy institute

explanation.surface: Someone is taken on to keep the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane rented privately is described so, and in Britain so is a fully qualified member of an accountancy body.
